subject.title: Install ClawHub packages for new Claw agents

question: Should experimental `claws add` be allowed to install or reuse a process-wide shared plugin when the exact plugin action, runtime identity, and artifact integrity are shown in a consent-bound plan?
rationale: The implementation can enforce an approved policy mechanically, but it cannot determine whether exact-plan consent is a sufficient authorization boundary for a shared runtime resource rather than a per-agent capability.

options.title: Approve exact-plan shared-host consent
options.body: Keep the proposed plugin path, provided the final proof demonstrates live install or reuse and maintainers accept that the action affects the shared host.

options.title: Limit this slice to workspace skills
options.body: Keep skill installation and provenance, but defer plugin package mutation until a host-level grant or stronger isolation model is designed.

options.title: Pause package mutation
options.body: Retain read-only package planning only until the broader RFC and lifecycle stack settle on ownership and recovery behavior.

recommendation.title: Approve exact-plan shared-host consent
recommendation.body: Keep the proposed plugin path, provided the final proof demonstrates live install or reuse and maintainers accept that the action affects the shared host.

likelyOwner.reason: Their review establishes the package-lifecycle invariants that the remaining authorization decision must satisfy.
